clue.text: Wine covered by company card

indicators.note: something covered by another has it wrapped over it

blocks.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A firm's corporate card being spent on wine.
explanation.walkthrough: PLC is the British label for a public limited company, the counterpart of Inc.
explanation.definitionFit: The material a credit card is made of has become everyday slang for the card itself, as in 'pay with ...'.

clue.text: So precentor moved into part of abbey

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted out of their places into a new order

explanation.surface: The choir's precentor has been transferred to a different corner of the abbey.
explanation.walkthrough: A precentor leads the singing in a cathedral or abbey, so the surface never leaves the church, which is exactly where the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: A named area of the south transept of Westminster Abbey, where many writers are buried or remembered: a definition by example.

clue.text: In hot capital councillor is in cooler area

blocks.note: air conditioning, which cools a room
Cr is the abbreviation for councillor
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A local councillor escapes a sweltering capital by sitting somewhere cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is a noun here, the air conditioner, not a comparison with the hot capital. Cr for councillor is a British abbreviation, as in Cr Smith.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana's capital lies a few degrees north of the equator and is hot all year, so 'hot capital' is a fair description.

clue.text: After meal, Carol is flirting

indicators.note: after means following in sequence

blocks.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: After dinner, a woman called Carol is flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes Carol look like a name; here it is the verb, to sing joyfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful mockery is a standard way of flirting, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Computer reading card, about to gain knowledge

blocks.note: a card is an eccentric, amusing person

explanation.surface: A computer scanning a card, on the point of learning something.
explanation.walkthrough: The card in the scanner is really the old sense of an odd, amusing person, 'a real card'.
explanation.definitionFit: The technology by which a computer reads printed or handwritten letters from a scanned image.

clue.text: Support pert somersault

blocks.note: flip, short for flippant, means pert

explanation.surface: A cheeky gymnast's somersault, deserving of support.
explanation.walkthrough: Flip as an adjective, cheeky or glib, is the less familiar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular somersault, turned backwards in the air: a definition by example.

clue.text: Kitty holding up curtains where she can’t see clearly?

indicators.note: in a down clue, what holds something up sits beneath it

blocks.note: a kitty is a pool of shared money

explanation.surface: A cat climbing the curtains, from where she can't see properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a cat; it is the pool of money. 'She' in the definition keeps the cat picture going, and the question mark admits the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The area outside someone's view, literally in driving or figuratively in judgement, is where they can't see clearly.

clue.text: Singer’s short section of poem

indicators.note: a word that is short is missing a bit

blocks.note: the singer is the one who leads prayers in a synagogue, cut by one letter at the end

explanation.surface: A singer's brief part in a long poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer is a CANTOR, and the 's stands for 'is': the singer is short, not the singer owning something.
explanation.definitionFit: Long poems such as Dante's Divine Comedy are divided into these main sections.

clue.text: Rock from Florida reproduced on stage

indicators.note: reproduced means made again, here in a new form, so the letters are remade in another order

blocks.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

explanation.surface: A rock brought from Florida and copied as scenery in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words 'on stage' run together as one block of anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat slab of sandstone used for paving is a kind of rock.

clue.text: Slight suspicion bell-like sound is out of tune at the start

indicators.note: a letter that is out has been taken away

blocks.note: the light ringing of a small bell
the first letter of tune, removed

explanation.surface: A vague feeling that a bell's chime sounds off-key at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of tune' reads as one musical phrase; split it: T is out, and 'tune at the start' names which letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a faint notion or hint that something is so.

clue.text: Dressed down (not personal) after impudent language

indicators.note: after means following in sequence

explanation.surface: Someone was dressed down, not personally, after cheeking a superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed down' looks like one phrase for a telling-off; the definition is only 'Dressed', in the kitchen sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad or dish that is dressed has had a sauce or dressing poured over it.

clue.text: In the company of doctor, consumed by anxiety

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed inside it

explanation.surface: A doctor overwhelmed by worry while keeping company.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, medical officer, is a stock crossword doctor alongside DR and GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be in the midst of a group is to be in its company.

clue.text: One on warhorse roughly arrested, first to be put in jail

explanation.surface: A cavalryman roughly arrested and the first to be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One on warhorse' paints a rider; it is the ornamental cloth laid on the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorated cloth spread over a medieval warhorse is something that sits on it.

clue.text: Daughter, yelling, led cast in Christmas scene

indicators.note: cast letters are thrown, like a die, and land in a new order

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A shouting daughter leads the cast of a Christmas nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the farm in Dickens's Pickwick Papers where Mr Pickwick spends a famous Christmas; 'cast' fits the nativity-play picture but only mixes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Wardle's farm hosts the Christmas festivities in The Pickwick Papers, so it is a scene of Christmas in fiction.

clue.text: Shrieks from former silent type bodging a minor task

indicators.note: bodging is doing a clumsy, botched job, so the letters come out mangled

blocks.note: someone who says nothing, clams up

explanation.surface: A once-quiet person yelps while fumbling a small job.
explanation.walkthrough: Shriek is old printers' slang for the punctuation mark, so the yelps are on paper. To bodge is British for doing a job badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers called the ! a shriek, so shrieks is a jargon name for the marks.

clue.text: With sudden action one clipped ticket

indicators.note: clipped means trimmed, so one loses its last letter

blocks.note: a sudden stroke, especially a seizure of power

explanation.surface: Someone swiftly snips out a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' suggests cutting a voucher out of a newspaper; it is trimming the E off 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher entitling the holder to goods or a discount is a kind of ticket.

clue.text: African insists sofa is ordered for Italian patron

indicators.note: ordered letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An African customer demands a sofa be ordered for an Italian client.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' belongs to the fodder, not the link: without it the letters come up two short.
explanation.definitionFit: The friar from Umbria is one of the two patron saints of Italy.

clue.text: Guru in India took to the water first

indicators.note: first means before the rest, so the swimming comes before the I

blocks.note: someone who went for a swim took to the water
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian holy man went for a swim before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guru in India' reads as the definition; India is only the letter I, which the swimming comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious teacher is a guru, a close synonym.

clue.text: Difficult pair in a hurry abandoning hotel

blocks.note: Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet, removed

explanation.surface: An awkward couple rushing to check out of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair lands after the R, splitting what is left of the rush, not at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hard, needing great effort.

clue.text: After July briefly in the country cutting introduction for important speech

indicators.note: briefly means in short form
cutting the introduction removes the first letter

blocks.note: RURAL (of the country) without its first letter

explanation.surface: An address delivered in the countryside in August, trimmed of its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The lone 'in' goes first in the answer although 'After July' leads the clue. 'The country' stands for the adjective, of the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, it is the address given by someone taking office, such as a US president, an important speech.

clue.text: Interrupting work, managed to grab one insect

blocks.note: op, opus, is a musical work
to run a business is to manage it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boss breaks off from work to catch a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the crossword's usual work. The answer is a common British butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A white butterfly whose males have orange wingtips; a butterfly is an insect, a definition by example.

clue.text: Lover embracing Mike is tense, for a Greek

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms round

blocks.note: a past tense of Greek verbs
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A lover holding Mike is nervous about a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like nervous; it is grammar, the aorist tense of ancient Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to love and love affairs is a lover, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Criminal’s worn out weapon

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered

explanation.surface: A villain's well-used firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' reads as one phrase; out is the anagram indicator acting on worn alone.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a bad character, someone on the wrong side of the law.

clue.text: Mangle words, just taking the opening caller

explanation.surface: Someone twisting words by only answering the first phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: Mangle looks like a verb for garbling words; it is the noun, the old roller machine for washing day.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangle is a pair of rollers that squeezes water out of wet laundry, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Bad-tempered match ending in affray

explanation.surface: An ill-tempered game that finishes in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket match lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: irritable, quick to take offence.

clue.text: What would make goose go in trap?

indicators.note: the letter N goes in where the G was

blocks.note: the word goose with its G taken out

explanation.surface: A riddle about coaxing a goose into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the G of goose for an N and you get a snare that a goose might indeed walk into.
explanation.definitionFit: A running loop of rope used to snare animals is a trap.

clue.text: Revealing taste of English joint with walnuts regularly added

indicators.note: regularly means at regular intervals
added means put on the end

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a joint of meat, as a leg of lamb
the second, fourth and sixth letters of walnuts

explanation.surface: A tasty English roast with walnuts thrown in at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taste' and 'joint' suggest a roast dinner; the taste is refinement, and the joint is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and graceful things show good taste, so the definition describes the adjective.

clue.text: Sellers opening in radio, earliest broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Shops advertising their launch on the radio at the first opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the radio picture but is only telling you to scatter the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers who sell goods to the public are sellers, a plain synonym.

clue.text: This is how defenders’ bureaucracy lifted doomed city

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means raised upward

blocks.note: the MoD, the British Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: A comment on how the defence bureaucracy rescued a doomed city.
explanation.walkthrough: The MoD is Britain's Ministry of Defence, the defenders' bureaucracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Genesis destroyed by fire and brimstone is the archetypal doomed city.

clue.text: Move impatiently, suggesting a few sips of a pint?

definitions.text: a few sips of a pint

blocks.clueFragment: a few sips of a pint
blocks.note: a fluid measure, abbreviated fl. oz. in full, a small fraction of a pint

explanation.surface: Someone stalks off in a huff after only a few sips of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as FL OUNCE, the fluid ounce: a British pint holds twenty, so one is a few sips. The question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm off in an exaggerated, impatient huff; and split in two, the word reads as a fluid ounce.

clue.text: Slope written about, nothing serious: one leads to attractive hill

blocks.note: a bad accident is a serious one
I is the Roman numeral one
the first letters of attractive and hill

explanation.surface: A slope noted as not serious, one route up an attractive hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Slope is not a gradient but Mr Slope, the scheming chaplain in Trollope's Barchester Towers, so 'Slope written about' is a character in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Slope's first name in Trollope's Barchester Towers, so the answer is the Slope an author wrote about.

clue.text: Full of energy, I bombard regiment heads to create disturbance

indicators.note: to head something is to go in front

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gunner full of beans describes shelling at the head of his regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of energy' sounds like pep; it wraps the bombardment round an E. 'Heads' says where the regiment goes, not that initials are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for making a loud fuss or uproar, a disturbance.

clue.text: Office in Parliament House announced for some

indicators.note: announced means spoken, and for some admits the match works only in accents that drop the R

blocks.note: the upper House of the British Parliament

explanation.surface: An office inside a parliament building, mentioned to a few people.
explanation.walkthrough: Office is the church's daily round of prayer, not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The dawn service of praise is one of the canonical hours of the Divine Office.

clue.text: Paper set by an individual mentor

blocks.note: jelly that has set has gelled

explanation.surface: An exam paper set by one person's tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper set' looks like an exam; the paper is a newspaper, and set is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit believed to watch over one particular person, or anyone who guides them, is that individual's mentor.

clue.text: Checked car, note tiny bit of damage

indicators.note: the tiniest bit of a word is a single letter, its first

blocks.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A car was inspected and a small scratch noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like writing something down; it is the musical note, as in do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that have been officially inspected have been checked.

clue.text: Expression of goodwill to pen instant message

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, as sheep in a pen

explanation.surface: A friendly note to write a quick online message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expression of goodwill' reads as one phrase for a kind word; only 'Expression' is the definition, the face you pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted face of pain or disgust is one kind of facial expression.

clue.text: Was too clever for overdue amount to be revised

indicators.note: revised text is rewritten, so the letters are rewritten in a new order

explanation.surface: A debtor's clever trick of getting an overdue bill rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about money; the definition is a past-tense verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone by cleverer moves is to be too clever for them.

clue.text: Use art to work with the score?

definitions.text: Use art to work with the score?

indicators.note: to work a material is to knead it into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A musician applying creative skill to a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: arranging music for an orchestra is using art on a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging a score for the instruments of a band takes musical art, so the whole clue reads straight.

clue.text: Operator’s face in part is caught in tangle

blocks.note: a tangled mass, as of hair

explanation.surface: A worker's face partly snagged in a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face in part' does not hide letters; it describes one feature of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a machine, such as a sewing machine, is its operator.

clue.text: Filled with runs, marquee game — here?

definitions.text: Filled with runs, marquee game — here?

blocks.note: a marquee is a large tent
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket match with lots of runs and hospitality marquees.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Test cricket ground in Nottingham, where runs are scored and marquees go up, so the whole clue also points at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham's Test cricket ground hosts high-scoring games with marquees, so the whole clue reads straight.

clue.text: Humble Charles X?

blocks.note: the short written form of Charles
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A modest French king, Charles the Tenth.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles X was a real king of France, so the regnal number reads as part of his name rather than a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue someone's pride is to humble them, used as a verb.

clue.text: Tons loaded into a slow vehicle, one with drawing power

blocks.note: a farm vehicle, slow on the road
t is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Heavy weights piled onto a tractor, a machine built to pull.
explanation.walkthrough: A tractor draws a plough, so 'drawing power' fits the surface too; the answer is anything that attracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that draws others towards it has drawing power.

clue.text: Not always very satisfied with back half

blocks.note: a demand that is met is satisfied

explanation.surface: A footballer who is only occasionally content playing at half-back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back half' looks like a football position; back reverses the prefix meaning half.
explanation.definitionFit: On some occasions but not others, a plain synonym for 'not always'.

clue.text: Pea, one shot with force into carpet

blocks.note: what is shot from a bow
F is the symbol for force

explanation.surface: A pea fired hard into a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a large dried pea, the base of British mushy peas.
explanation.definitionFit: A large variety of pea, so the definition is by type.

clue.text: Person on podium departs, absorbed by menu?

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is soaked up inside it

blocks.note: a menu is a list for a meal, a meal list
d is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A speaker on stage leaves, engrossed in the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'menu' is being described loosely rather than defined.
explanation.definitionFit: An Olympic winner stands on the podium to be given a prize.

clue.text: Pull hard — bliss to stop short

indicators.note: to stop short is to halt before the end, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: An instruction to tug hard, as happiness comes to an abrupt end.
explanation.walkthrough: Bliss is paradise, a six-letter word that loses its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul with great effort is to pull hard.

clue.text: For lawyer, preclude missing most of best opportunity

indicators.note: most of the phrase is missing, leaving a short run from inside it

blocks.note: the run of letters from the second to the sixth

explanation.surface: A lawyer blocks a case, losing most of the best chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is legal jargon, so the clue tags it 'for lawyer'.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to bar someone from asserting something is to preclude them.

clue.text: Crowd keenly ready for exercise

blocks.note: someone up for it is keen and ready

explanation.surface: A gym class of people eager for a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the British name for a push-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing the body up from the floor with the arms is a standard exercise, a definition by example.

clue.text: Leader of crusade can’t supply revolutionary

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A crusade leader unable to provide a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like provide; it is the adverb of supple, flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norman prince who led troops in the First Crusade and took part in capturing Jerusalem.

clue.text: French team at first rehearsing opening number of positive value perhaps

indicators.note: at first means at the start

blocks.note: n is the symbol for a number
French for eleven, the size of a football or cricket side
the first letters of rehearsing and opening

explanation.surface: A French side rehearsing its opening number before a show.
explanation.walkthrough: A team is an eleven, and eleven in French is ONZE. The 'perhaps' is there because negative numbers qualify too.
explanation.definitionFit: Any positive value is not nothing, so it is an example of the answer; the 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Delay agitation by lower-classes

blocks.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification

explanation.surface: A hold-up caused by unrest among the working classes.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research sorts people into social grades A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so D and E are the lower classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A postponement is a delay, a plain synonym.

clue.text: The town of Stone put in working order

blocks.note: the order in which people take turns at work

explanation.surface: A town called Stone being put in working order.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone looks like a town name (there is a Stone in Staffordshire); it is the famous inscribed Stone in the British Museum, named after the Egyptian town where it was found.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian port where the trilingual Stone was found in 1799 gave the Stone its name.

clue.text: Business less successful, move to smaller premises

blocks.note: business that is down is doing worse

explanation.surface: A struggling firm relocating to a smaller office.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a single business story; it splits cleanly after 'successful'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for selling up and moving to somewhere smaller or cheaper.

clue.text: Eye old phone in Texas, America

blocks.note: o is the abbreviation for old
the American word for a mobile phone

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing an old telephone in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Texas' flags American usage: a mobile phone has a different name there.
explanation.definitionFit: The simple light-sensing eye of an insect, or an eye-like spot on a wing: a technical word for an eye.

clue.text: Bear doing without originally regular supply

indicators.note: to do without something is to manage without it, so a letter is left out
originally means at the origin

blocks.note: the first letter of regular, removed

explanation.surface: A bear going without its regular food supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Bear looks like the animal; it is the verb, to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone with a quality is to supply them with it, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Tease our folk about money

indicators.note: about means turned round, as in about-face, so both pieces are read backwards

explanation.surface: Teasing one's own family about money.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both pieces together, not just the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for money, as the sweet stuff everyone wants.

clue.text: High tension apparatus turned a distance round

indicators.note: something turned is spun round to face the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: the initial letters of high tension

explanation.surface: High-voltage equipment rotated a long way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'round' in the definition belongs with the measurement; the turning is done by 'turned'.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement around the middle of something is a distance round it.

clue.text: Performer to pose around inside facility

blocks.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A performer strikes a pose inside a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' looks like a building; it is facility as a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Singers and actors are called artistes or recording stars, so any performer fits by extension.

clue.text: Set firm deadlines, strangely not inflicted by anyone else

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A person strangely imposes strict deadlines on themselves alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer nicely: deadlines you set yourself come from nobody else.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given or imposed by oneself is not inflicted by anyone else.

clue.text: With time moving on, catch is transported

explanation.surface: Over time, someone who is caught gets carried off.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the T slides two places on.
explanation.definitionFit: Carried away with delight, which is the rapturous sense of transported.

clue.text: Most crazy youngsters go here, taken at first

indicators.note: at first means at the start

explanation.surface: The wildest children go here when they're taken.
explanation.walkthrough: Potty is British for mildly crazy, and a potty is also a child's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a British word for crazy, so the most crazy.

clue.text: Novel Russian garden

explanation.surface: A new style of Russian garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like new; it is the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott's 1819 romance of a Saxon knight is a novel, a definition by example.
